content:
andrew: seeing a sudden spike of 503s for hosted-infer in us-west-2 starting ~08:12 UTC. multiple customer complaints about timeouts and retries.
maya: alerts show upstream runner exits with SIGSEGV and OOM messages around the same time. paging now.
maya: dmesg snippet: ```Apr 22 08:12:33 runner[21345]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f9b... sp 00007fffdc...
Kernel panic-like OOM: Out of memory: Killed process 21345 (infer-runner) total-vm: 120000000kB anonymous
```
julian: i started a quick repro locally — hit with a long-chat prompt (context ~18k tokens) and saw kv_cache size grow rapidly until allocation failures then segfault on our attention kernel.
emily (support): customer reported 4 failed requests then retries; they say they saw duplicate charges for some of the retries. ticket INC-12345 opened and escalated.
andrew: probable path: new kv-prefetch + attention kernel regression causing unchecked vmalloc growth and then eventual SIGSEGV when a follow-up allocation touches freed memory.
maya: mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from affected pool, 2) enable fallback to cpu-backed runners for impacted customers, 3) throttle large-context requests, 4) roll runtime back to 0.9.6 on canary.
julian: i can push a canary rollback and add a runtime guard that refuses kv prefetch above 12GB. will need a quick CI build.
andrew: also want runtime core + gdb backtrace before excessive cleanup. collect: ```gdb --batch -ex 'thread apply all bt' -ex 'quit' /opt/runner/bin/infer-runner core```, ```kubectl logs -n hosted runner-abc --previous```, ```sudo journalctl -k | tail -n 200```.
maya: gathering cores and logs from affected hosts now; attaching kube artifacts to the incident.
julian: pasted minimal backtrace from core: ```#0 0x7f9b23a in attention_forward()
#1 0x7f8a12c in kv_prefetch_thread
#2 0x7f7b001 in start_thread``` suggests crash inside the optimized attention path after prefetch.
emily (support): told customer we are failing over traffic and applying a rollback; offered a credit for retries and suggested switching to dedicated capacity if they need SLAs. they accepted temporary failover.
andrew: short-term plan: rollback runtime to 0.9.6 on canary (10% traffic) + enable fallback routing for tenants showing >3 failures in 5m, add request-size throttle for context >12k tokens.
maya: implemented alert rule: runner_restarts > 5 within 10m and vmalloc_used_pct > 80% -> P1. also added grafana panel for kvcache bytes per runner.
julian: pushed canary rollback and guard; monitoring shows canary runners stable for last 6m. preparing PR for 0.9.8 with proper memory caps and safe prefetch.
andrew: ask SRE to review kernel vmalloc reserve tweak? prefer not to touch host-level kernel unless necessary.
maya: agreed — avoid kernel changes in prod. prefer runtime-level caps.
emily (support): closing loop with customer, will update INC-12345 after final rollout.
andrew: next actions: (a) merge 0.9.8 PR with mem cap & prefetch checks, (b) expand rollback to full pool if stability holds for 30m, (c) postmortem after root-cause confirmed.
emily (support): :thumbsup: assigning follow-ups in the ticket and will request billing credit for duplicate charge window.
sre-bot: note: fallback routing applied to tenant-42 at 08:25 UTC, rollback canary promoted at 08:32 UTC.
andrew: thanks team — keeping this thread open until postmortem doc published.
